note: Source article definitions for generate_knowledge_base.py. Chunk text is hashed verbatim into the corpus; edit here, then regenerate.
windows_scope: Windows 10 22H2 (restricted support: requires enterprise ESU or a supported LTSC lifecycle)

articles.title: Outlook for Windows will not start or hangs on the splash screen
symptoms: Outlook stops at 'Loading Profile'
the window never appears
Outlook closes immediately after launch

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the affected device, the Windows edition and feature release, and whether the employee uses classic Outlook or new Outlook. On Windows 10 without enterprise ESU or a supported LTSC lifecycle, only restricted diagnostics and migration guidance apply.
chunks.Read-only checks: With diagnostic consent, inspect running processes for a stuck OUTLOOK.EXE, review the last application error in Event Viewer, and check whether Outlook starts in safe mode. None of these steps change configuration or read message content.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: The most common causes are a faulty COM add-in, a corrupt navigation-pane or profile setting, and a pending Office update that did not finish. A clean start in safe mode that succeeds points to an add-in or profile fault.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Propose one exact change at a time: disable a single named add-in, reset the navigation pane, or complete the pending Office update. Capture the pre-change state first so the step can be rolled back. The change is applied only after the employee approves it.
chunks.Verification: After the change, launch Outlook normally and confirm it reaches the inbox. Ask the employee to confirm they can open and send a message before the incident is closed.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows crashes intermittently during normal use
symptoms: Outlook closes without warning
'Microsoft Outlook has stopped working'
crashes when opening a specific item

chunks.Confirm the scope: Establish when the crash happens (on launch, on send, when opening an attachment) and how often. Record the Outlook build and the Windows feature release.
chunks.Read-only checks: Review the faulting-module name in the Windows application error log and list installed COM add-ins with their publishers. Compare the add-in list with the approved baseline. These checks do not alter the client.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A repeatable faulting module that belongs to a third-party add-in indicates an add-in fault. Crashes only when rendering messages can indicate a graphics or hardware-acceleration issue.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Candidate changes, each applied singly and reversibly after approval: disable the implicated add-in, turn off hardware graphics acceleration, or repair the Office installation. The prior setting is recorded so it can be restored.
chunks.Verification: Reproduce the original workflow that crashed and confirm it now completes. Close the incident only after the employee confirms the task works.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows shows Disconnected or Trying to connect
symptoms: status bar reads Disconnected
mail is not sending or receiving
connection recovers then drops again

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the device and whether other network applications work. Identify whether the mailbox is Exchange Online or on-premises Exchange, and whether a VPN is in use.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, run read-only network checks: name resolution for the mail endpoint, proxy configuration, and the Outlook connection-status view. Confirm the device clock is accurate. No settings are changed.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Frequent causes are broken name resolution, an incorrect or stale proxy, a captive-portal or VPN split-tunnel problem, and a corrupt cached-mode data file. A device that fails only on this network points to DNS or proxy.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Proposed reversible changes: correct the proxy setting, refresh the network profile, or rebuild the offline cache file after backing up the existing one. Each is explained and applied only on approval, with the previous state captured for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the status returns to Connected and a test message sends and is received. The employee confirms normal mail flow before closure.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows repeatedly prompts for a password
symptoms: the credential prompt reappears after entry
'Need Password' in the status bar
sign-in loop

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the account shown in the prompt and whether the employee can sign in to the same account in a browser. Do not ask for or record the password.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the stored credential entries for the mail service, the modern-authentication state of the client, and the account's connection status. Reviewing which entries exist does not expose secret values.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Typical causes are a stale cached credential, a client that is not using modern authentication, a broken token-broker state on the device, or a Conditional Access requirement that Outlook cannot satisfy in its current state.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates, one at a time after approval: remove the stale stored credential entry so the account can re-authenticate, restart the token broker, or repair the Office identity state. Identity administration and policy changes are out of scope and are escalated.
chunks.Verification: Confirm Outlook connects without prompting and stays connected through a send and receive. The employee confirms the prompt no longer appears.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows mailbox or calendar is not synchronising
symptoms: new mail appears on phone but not in Outlook
calendar updates are missing
'This folder was last updated' is hours old

chunks.Confirm the scope: Identify the folders affected (inbox, a shared folder, calendar) and whether the problem is one folder or the whole mailbox. Confirm the device and client type.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, review the folder update times, the send/receive group configuration, cached-mode settings, and the local data-file size against the mailbox quota. These are inspection-only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Causes include a paused send/receive group, a cached-mode download window that excludes older items, a data file near its size limit, and a single corrupt item blocking the sync queue.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: resume or correct the send/receive group, widen the cached-mode window, or move the blocking item aside. The current configuration is captured so it can be restored.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the affected folders update to current and a newly sent test item appears within the expected interval. The employee confirms their mail and calendar are current.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows offline data file (.ost) is corrupt or oversized
symptoms: 'Outlook data file cannot be accessed'
the .ost file will not open
search and folders behave inconsistently

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the account uses cached Exchange mode so the .ost can be safely rebuilt from the server copy. Record the current file path and size.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the data-file status in account settings, the file size against the supported limit, and the last successful synchronisation time. No file is modified during inspection.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: An .ost that exceeds the supported size, was interrupted mid-write, or sits on a synced or network location commonly becomes inconsistent. Because the server holds the authoritative copy, a rebuilt .ost restores content.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, rename the existing .ost so Outlook creates a fresh one and re-downloads from the server. The old file is retained, not deleted, so the step is reversible.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the new .ost finishes its initial synchronisation and the folder counts match the server. The employee confirms their mail is complete and searchable.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows personal data file (.pst) reports errors
symptoms: 'errors have been detected in the file'
an archive or personal folder will not open
items disappear from a .pst folder

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm which .pst is affected and its purpose (archive, export, local-only folders). Unlike an .ost, a .pst has no server copy, so a verified backup is required before any repair.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, record the .pst path, size, and whether it is stored on a local disk or a redirected or synced folder. Confirm a current backup exists. Inspection does not open or alter the file.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A .pst on a network or continuously synced location, or one closed uncleanly, is prone to header inconsistency. Very large legacy .pst files are also more fragile.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After a backup is confirmed and the employee approves, run the built-in Inbox Repair tool against a copy of the file, then attach the repaired copy. The original is preserved for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the repaired .pst opens, folder counts are intact, and a sample of items is readable. The employee confirms the folders they need are present.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows search returns no or incomplete results
symptoms: 'Something went wrong and your search couldn't be completed'
recent mail is not found
search works in one folder only

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether search fails everywhere or only in specific folders, and whether the employee searches the current mailbox or 'All Mailboxes'. Record the Windows feature release.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, review Windows Search indexing status, the Outlook indexing-locations list, and whether the service is running. Confirm how much of the mailbox reports as indexed. These checks are read-only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are an incomplete or paused index, Outlook missing from the indexed-locations list, a cached-mode window that excludes older mail, and a corrupt index database.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: add Outlook back to the indexed locations, widen the cached-mode window, or rebuild the search index. The current settings are recorded first.
chunks.Verification: After the index reports complete, confirm a known recent and a known old message are both found. The employee confirms search returns what they expect.

articles.title: Outlook for Windows is slow, freezes, or shows 'Not Responding'
symptoms: long pauses when switching folders
'Not Responding' during send/receive
high memory use by OUTLOOK.EXE

chunks.Confirm the scope: Establish when the slowness occurs and whether it correlates with send/receive, a large folder, or a specific add-in. Record the client build and available device memory.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, review add-in load times, the size and item counts of the largest folders, the data-file size against its limit, and whether a third-party antivirus is scanning the data file. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Frequent contributors are a slow add-in, an oversized single folder, a data file near its size limit, and real-time scanning of the .ost or .pst by security software.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: disable the slow add-in, help the employee file or archive items from the oversized folder, or add the data file to the security-software exclusion list per policy. Prior state is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm folder switching and send/receive complete within a normal interval. The employee confirms Outlook feels responsive for their daily tasks.

articles.title: A Windows device cannot find or add the expected printer
symptoms: the printer is not in the Add a printer list
'Windows can't connect to the printer'
the mapped printer disappeared

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the printer's identity and expected connection (direct TCP/IP, print server queue, or Windows protected print). Confirm the employee is on the network segment that can reach it.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check name resolution and reachability for the printer or print server, the list of installed printers and their ports, and whether the print server queue is published. No configuration is changed.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Typical causes are the device being on a different VLAN or VPN state, a removed or renamed print-server queue, a missing driver, or Windows protected print mode filtering an unsupported connection.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: re-add the correct print-server queue, create the correct TCP/IP port, or install the approved driver package. The prior printer configuration is captured for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the printer appears and a test page prints. The employee confirms a real document prints from the application they use.

articles.title: A printer shows Offline on a Windows device
symptoms: the printer status reads Offline
jobs sit in the queue and do not print
the printer works from other devices

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether the printer is offline for one device or all devices, and its connection type. If other devices print, the fault is local to this device or its path to the printer.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check reachability to the printer or server, the 'Use Printer Offline' flag, the port configuration, and whether SNMP status is being misread. These are inspection steps only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are the manual 'Use Printer Offline' setting, a printer that changed IP address, an SNMP status query the printer answers slowly, and a sleeping network printer.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: clear the offline flag, correct the port address, or disable SNMP status on the port. The prior settings are recorded so they can be restored.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the status returns to Ready and a queued job completes. The employee confirms the pages they expected are produced.

articles.title: Print jobs are stuck in the Windows print queue
symptoms: a job shows 'Deleting - Printing' and never clears
new jobs pile up behind a stuck job
'Document stuck in print queue'

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the queue name and whether the stuck job is on this device or on a shared print server, because clearing a server queue affects other users.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, list the queued jobs and their states, check the print spooler service status, and check free space on the spool volume. Inspection does not remove jobs.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A malformed job, a spooler that has stopped, a full spool volume, or a driver fault commonly wedge the queue. One job in an error state usually blocks the rest.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, remove the specific blocking job, and if required restart the print spooler service after noting the current job list. On a shared server this is coordinated so other users' jobs are preserved where possible.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the queue drains and a fresh test job prints. The employee confirms their document prints correctly.

articles.title: The Windows Print Spooler service is not running or keeps stopping
symptoms: 'The print spooler service is not running'
no printers are listed
the spooler stops again shortly after starting

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm no printers appear and that the fault is the spooler rather than a single queue. Record the Windows feature release and recent driver or update changes.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the spooler service state and start type, the application error log for the faulting module, and the contents of the spool folder for a large or malformed job. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A single corrupt spool file, a faulty third-party print driver, or a dependency service that is not running commonly cause repeated spooler stops.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval and after recording the current job list, clear the specific corrupt spool file, then start the spooler. If a named driver is implicated, roll it back to the approved package through the governed driver workflow.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the spooler stays running, printers reappear, and a test page prints. The employee confirms printing works for their normal documents.

articles.title: A TCP/IP printer port on Windows fails or points to the wrong address
symptoms: 'The printer could not be found' after a network change
jobs fail with a port error
printing is slow then times out

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the printer's current network address and the address configured on the Windows port. A recent DHCP change or device replacement often explains a mismatch.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, compare the configured port address with the printer's actual address, test reachability and the print port, and check the SNMP setting on the port. No change is made during inspection.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: The port address is stale after the printer's IP changed, the port uses a protocol the printer no longer accepts, or SNMP status polling on the port is failing.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, correct the port to the printer's reserved address or switch it to a hostname, and disable SNMP status if it is unreliable. The prior port configuration is captured for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm a test page prints promptly and the status is Ready. The employee confirms documents print without delay.

articles.title: Printing through a Windows print server fails for a device
symptoms: 'Windows cannot connect to the printer' with an error code
the server queue is greyed out
only server-hosted printers fail

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm which server queue fails and whether other users of the same queue are affected. A server-wide fault is escalated to the print-server owner rather than fixed on the endpoint.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check reachability to the print server, whether the queue is published and shared, the client's cached connection to the queue, and the driver the queue offers versus what is installed locally. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A stale client-side connection, a driver-architecture or point-and-print mismatch, or a server-side queue or spooler problem are the usual causes.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: For endpoint-scoped causes, after approval: remove and re-add the server queue, or install the approved matching driver locally. Server-side causes are escalated with the collected evidence.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the queue connects and a test page prints through the server. The employee confirms their documents print.

articles.title: A printer driver on Windows is missing, mismatched, or broken after an update
symptoms: garbled output or wrong page sizes
'Driver is unavailable'
printing broke after a Windows or driver update

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the printer model, the installed driver name and version, and whether the problem began after a specific update. Note whether the model relies on a third-party driver affected by servicing changes.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, record the installed driver and its date, compare it with the approved package, and check whether Windows substituted an inbox or IPP-class driver. Inspection does not change the driver.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A Windows update replaced a vendor driver with a class driver, a third-party driver reached end of servicing, or the installed driver does not match the printer's page description language.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, install or roll back to the approved driver package through the governed driver workflow, capturing the current driver first so the change is reversible.
chunks.Verification: Confirm a test page and a representative document print with correct layout and colour. The employee confirms output quality is back to normal.

articles.title: Windows protected print mode blocks an older printer or connection
symptoms: a previously working printer cannot be added
'This printer isn't supported' in protected print mode
only IPP/Mopria printers work

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether Windows protected print mode is enabled on the device and whether the target printer supports IPP or Mopria. Protected print mode intentionally restricts non-standard drivers.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the protected-print setting state, the printer's supported protocols, and whether an IPP path to the printer or its server exists. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: The printer relies on a legacy third-party driver that protected print mode does not allow, or it is reachable only through a non-IPP port.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Preferred reversible change after approval: add the printer over IPP or through a print server that presents it as IPP. Changing the protected-print setting itself is a policy decision and is referred to the device-policy owner.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the printer adds over the supported path and prints a test page. The employee confirms their documents print.

articles.title: A scanner is not detected by Windows
symptoms: the scanner is missing from Windows settings
'No scanners were detected'
the multifunction device prints but does not scan

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the scanner model and connection (USB or network), and whether it is a standalone scanner or the scan function of a multifunction device. Record the Windows feature release.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check whether the device appears in Device Manager or under network devices, the state of the imaging service, and for a network device its reachability. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Typical causes are a missing WIA-class or vendor driver, the imaging service stopped, a network scanner on a different segment, or a USB power or cable fault.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: install the approved scanner driver, start the imaging service, or add the network scanner by its reserved address. Prior state is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the scanner is listed and a test scan completes. The employee confirms they can scan the document type they need.

articles.title: The Windows Image Acquisition (WIA) service or a WIA scan fails
symptoms: 'The device is not ready' or a WIA error code
scanning starts then aborts
Windows Fax and Scan cannot use the device

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether any application can scan or only one, and whether the device works from the vendor's own utility. A device that scans from the vendor tool but not from Windows points to the WIA layer.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the WIA service and its dependencies, the WIA minidriver registration for the device, and the application error log for the failing component. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A stopped WIA service or dependency, a corrupt or unregistered minidriver, or another process holding the device commonly cause WIA scan failures.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: start the WIA service and its dependencies, reinstall the approved driver so the minidriver re-registers, or close the process holding the device. Prior state is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm a scan completes from Windows Fax and Scan and from the employee's normal application. The employee confirms scanning works.

articles.title: A scanner driver is missing or mismatched on Windows
symptoms: a yellow warning on the imaging device in Device Manager
scans are blank or wrong size
the driver disappeared after an update

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the exact model and the Windows architecture, and check whether the installed driver matches the device and architecture. Record whether the problem started after an update.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, record the installed imaging driver and version, compare it with the approved package, and check whether Windows substituted a generic driver. Inspection does not change the driver.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A Windows update replaced the vendor driver, the wrong architecture driver is installed, or the device needs both a WIA and a vendor component and only one is present.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, install or roll back to the approved driver package, capturing the current driver first so the change can be reversed.
chunks.Verification: Confirm a test scan produces a correctly sized, non-blank image. The employee confirms scan quality is acceptable.

articles.title: A scanner is locked or busy and cannot be used by an application
symptoms: 'The device is in use by another application'
scanning hangs until the vendor tool is closed
only the first scan after a reboot works

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm which applications need the scanner and whether a vendor utility or a previous scan session is still running. WIA and TWAIN both take an exclusive lock during a session.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, identify processes that have the imaging device open and check whether a prior scan dialog is still active in the background. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A vendor tray utility holding the device, a scan session that did not close cleanly, or two applications trying to acquire the device at once.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, close the specific process holding the lock, or set the vendor utility not to auto-start so it does not hold the device. Prior startup state is recorded for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the employee's application can start and finish a scan, then start another. The employee confirms repeated scanning works.

articles.title: A network scanner or scan-to-folder destination stops working
symptoms: scan to email or folder fails at the device
the network scanner is unreachable from Windows
scans stopped arriving after a network change

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether the scanner initiates the transfer (scan to folder or email) or the workstation pulls the scan, and confirm the destination path or address. A recent address or credential change on the destination is a common trigger.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, test reachability between the device and the destination, check the destination share or mailbox is reachable, and confirm the scanner's stored address is current. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: The scanner's IP changed, the scan-to-folder share moved or its permissions changed, or a firewall change blocked the transfer path.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, correct the scanner's reserved address or the destination path, or request the destination-share owner restore the required access. Endpoint changes capture prior state for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm a test scan reaches the destination. The employee confirms scans arrive where they expect them.

articles.title: Windows denies an application permission to use the scanner or camera
symptoms: 'Access to the scanner is denied'
the app cannot start a scan on a managed device
scanning works for one user profile but not another

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the Windows account in use and whether the app relies on the Windows camera or imaging privacy setting. Confirm the device is not in a restricted-support state.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the imaging or camera privacy setting for desktop apps, the account's membership for local device access, and whether a policy restricts the imaging device. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: The privacy setting for desktop apps is off, the account lacks local access to the device class, or a managed policy blocks it.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, enable the imaging privacy setting for desktop apps for the employee, or add the account to the correct local access as policy allows. Policy-enforced blocks are referred to the device-policy owner. Prior state is recorded.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the application can now scan. The employee confirms scanning works from their normal application and account.

articles.title: A Windows network adapter has no connection or a limited connection
symptoms: a red X or 'No Internet' on the network icon
the adapter shows 'Network cable unplugged' while connected
the adapter is disabled

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm which adapter is expected to be in use (Wi-Fi or Ethernet), whether any network works, and whether a docking station or USB adapter is involved. Record the Windows feature release.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the adapter status and driver state, the assigned IP configuration, and whether the adapter is administratively disabled. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are a disabled adapter, a failed or outdated adapter driver, a dock or cable fault, and a stale IP configuration with no valid gateway.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: enable the adapter, reset the adapter's IP configuration to obtain a fresh lease, or roll the adapter driver back to the approved version. Prior state is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the adapter reports a valid address and gateway and a known internal host responds. The employee confirms the applications they need now work.

articles.title: Windows Wi-Fi will not connect or drops repeatedly
symptoms: 'Can't connect to this network'
Wi-Fi connects then drops after a few minutes
the corporate SSID is not listed

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the SSID the employee should use, the location, and whether other devices in the same place connect. Record the adapter model and driver version.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, review the saved profile for the SSID, the signal level and band, the adapter driver state, and the wireless report for repeated disconnect events. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A stale or wrong saved profile, an outdated adapter driver, aggressive power management on the adapter, or weak signal and band steering commonly cause Wi-Fi problems.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: remove and recreate the saved profile for the SSID, turn off adapter power saving, or update the adapter driver to the approved version. Prior state is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the device stays connected through a sustained transfer and a known internal host responds. The employee confirms the connection is stable for their work.

articles.title: A Windows device fails to obtain a valid IP address
symptoms: an address starting 169.254 (APIPA)
'Unidentified network'
the device works only with a manual address

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether the device should use DHCP, whether other devices on the same segment get an address, and whether a static address was set previously. Record the adapter in use.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the current IP configuration, whether the address is APIPA, the DHCP lease state, and whether a static configuration is present. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are a leftover static configuration, a DHCP request not reaching the server (switch port, VLAN, or Wi-Fi association), and a scope with no free addresses.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: set the adapter back to automatic addressing, release and renew the lease, or reconnect to the correct network. If the DHCP scope is exhausted, the incident is escalated to the network owner. Prior settings are captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the device holds a valid lease with a gateway and DNS server, and an internal host responds. The employee confirms connectivity is restored.

articles.title: Name resolution fails on a Windows device while the network is up
symptoms: 'server DNS address could not be found' in the browser
an internal site fails by name but works by address
some names resolve and others do not

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the device has a valid address and gateway, and identify the names that fail versus those that work. A device that reaches hosts by address but not by name has a resolution problem, not a connectivity one.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the configured DNS servers, the DNS suffix and search list, and the resolver cache for stale or negative entries. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are wrong or unreachable DNS servers, a missing DNS suffix for internal names, a poisoned resolver cache, and a VPN state that did not apply the corporate DNS.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: restore automatic DNS from DHCP, correct the DNS suffix, or clear the resolver cache. VPN-applied DNS problems are addressed with the VPN client. Prior settings are captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the previously failing internal and external names now resolve and load. The employee confirms the sites and applications they need work by name.

articles.title: A Windows proxy setting blocks or misroutes traffic
symptoms: all web traffic fails while other apps work
'unable to connect to the proxy server'
traffic works on VPN but not off it, or vice versa

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm whether the environment uses an automatic proxy script, a manual proxy, or none, and whether the problem is on or off VPN. Record whether a manual proxy was set by hand.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, review the current proxy configuration, whether the automatic-configuration script location is reachable, and whether a stale manual proxy is set. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are a manual proxy left configured after leaving a network, an unreachable automatic-configuration script, and an automatic-proxy setting fighting a VPN's own proxy.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: remove the stale manual proxy, restore automatic detection or the correct script location, or align the setting with the VPN's requirement. Prior configuration is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm web traffic works both on and off VPN as expected for the environment. The employee confirms their browsing and web applications work.

articles.title: The Windows VPN client will not connect or breaks other connectivity
symptoms: the VPN fails with an error code
the VPN connects but internal resources are unreachable
internet stops while the VPN is connected

chunks.Confirm the scope: Confirm the VPN profile in use, whether the failure is at connect time or after connecting, and whether internal or external access is the problem. Confirm the underlying network works first.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, review the VPN profile settings, the client event log for the connection attempt, and after connecting the assigned routes and DNS. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: Common causes are an out-of-date or duplicate VPN profile, a client that needs an update, missing routes for split tunnel, and DNS that did not switch to corporate servers on connect.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: Reversible candidates after approval: recreate the VPN profile from the approved template, update the VPN client to the approved version, or refresh routes and DNS after connecting. Server-side authentication or gateway faults are escalated. Prior state is captured.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the VPN connects and both internal resources and, where expected, internet access work. The employee confirms they can reach what they need over the VPN.

articles.title: A required Windows networking service is stopped
symptoms: network features fail after a service was disabled
'Network List Service' or DHCP client not running
the network icon never leaves the connecting state

chunks.Confirm the scope: Identify the specific networking service implicated (for example the DHCP client, DNS client, WLAN service, or Network Location Awareness) and confirm the symptom matches that service's role.
chunks.Read-only checks: With consent, check the service state and start type, its dependencies, and the system log for why it stopped. Inspection only.
chunks.Evidence-based causes: A service left disabled by earlier troubleshooting, a failed dependency, or a policy that changed the start type are the usual causes.
chunks.Approval-gated remediation: After approval, set the service to its correct start type and start it, and start any stopped dependency first. The prior start type and state are recorded for rollback.
chunks.Verification: Confirm the service stays running and the dependent network feature works. The employee confirms the affected function is restored.
